en: Our national bird, the Philippine eagle, has a unique shaggy crest and is critically endangered, with only about four hundred individuals left in the wild.
Philippine independence was declared twice, first by Emilio Aguinaldo on June 12, 1898, and again when the United States granted it on July 4, 1946.
The Chief Justice of the Philippine Supreme Court must be at least forty years old and have served as a judge or lawyer for fifteen years.
The Ifugao people carved the magnificent Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains over two thousand years ago using only their bare hands and simple tools.
Filipino scientist Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a unique bamboo incubator for premature babies.
Before the Spanish arrived, early Filipinos wrote on bamboo using Baybayin, an ancient alphabet where every consonant automatically includes an 'a' vowel sound.
The sampaguita, our national flower, is not actually native to the Philippines but was introduced from China and officially declared our national flower in 1934.
During the Ati-Atihan festival in Aklan, dancers paint their skin black with soot to honor the indigenous Ati people who originally welcomed Malay settlers.
National hero Jose Rizal was a polymath who spoke twenty-two languages and secretly sculpted a small bust of a woman while exiled in Dapitan.
The Philippine Bill of Rights strictly prohibits the use of torture, force, or any means that violates the free will of a detained person.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan originated in rural areas where entire communities physically carried a family's nipa hut to a new location.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his massive and dramatic painting, Spoliarium.
